text:
Maya: heads-up — bringing up the hf-converted Llama2 variant on staging and seeing early termination in streaming when prompt contains system messages with trailing EOS.
Maya: repro steps: convert with `transformers` + tokenizer.save_pretrained -> our hf2redwood script -> upload. stream via SDK with stop_sequences=[""]
Maya: sample conversation payload:
```
role: system\ncontent: \"You are an assistant.\"\nrole: user\ncontent: \"Summarize: foo bar.\"\nstop: [\"\"]
```
Maya: stream output stops right after first sentence, even though model should produce 3 sentences. logs show token stream contained consecutive "" tokens mid-generation.
Raj: can you paste tokenizer config.json and special_tokens_map from the converted model?
Maya: pasted snippets:
```
{"eos_token": "", "bos_token": "<s>", "unk_token": "<unk>", "pad_token": "<pad>"}
// special_tokens_map.json
{"eos_token": "", "bos_token": "<s>"}
```
Maya: also tokenizer converted to r30_bpe, tokenization of the string "\n\n" yields `[50256, 50256]` (two eos ids).
Oliver: ah — hf tokenizer kept EOS as an explicit token id and the BPE encoder emits multiple EOS tokens for blank lines. streaming layer treats any encountered eos_id as termination, so consecutive eos ids cause immediate stop.
Eva: is this new compared to previous models? could be tokenizer behaviour change after tokenizer update/merging.
Maya: older models had eos as single sentinel; new tokenizer encodes empty lines as repeated eos ids. repro tokenization logs:
```
prompt: "Hello\n\n"
-> token ids: [15496, 13, 50256, 50256]
```
Raj: two obvious fixes: 1) post-process token stream to collapse repeated eos tokens before applying stop detection, or 2) change tokenizer config to map repeated blank-piece sequences to a single eos id during conversion.
Oliver: also check chat template: if we append system/user separators that end with an eos, template concatenation can introduce adjacent eos tokens (e.g., system ends with "" + user starts with "").
Maya: our conversion script left `add_prefix_space` default, and we didn't merge special tokens. here's convert snippet we used:
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
Tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(src)
Tok.save_pretrained(dest)
# our hf2redwood does minimal edits
```
Eva: quick mitigation: on streaming path set stop_sequence matching to string-level rather than id-level; i.e., inspect decoded chunk and only stop when the textual stop sequence appears, not on raw eos_id. That will avoid false-positive stops from split eos emission.
Raj: good idea. downside: adds latency for large vocab models if you wait to decode. but for staging it's fine.
Maya: tried that — switching to text-level detection fixed early stops but now we see trailing empty strings in final output (double EOS preserved).
Oliver: final output can be post-processed to trim repeated sentinel tokens and normalize trailing whitespace. also consider adding a small normalization step in the model card: `merge_consecutive_eos = true`.
Maya: opened a small experiment: re-tokenize training data with `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token': ''})` then run `tokenizer.train_new_from_iterator` to see if merges happen (results: fewer consecutive eos, but vocabulary drift).
Eva: Another angle — quantization experiments changed logits for eos token making it surface earlier in beam/greedy; any quant config applied?
Maya: we tested both fp16 and q4_0. q4 seemed slightly more eager on eos, but the big difference was tokenizer emitting multiple eos.
deploy-bot: uploaded converted package to s3://redwood-staging/models/llama2-hfconv-1765432100.tar.gz
Raj: action items: 1) Maya to add a short-term patch in streaming layer to collapse consecutive eos ids before stop check (PR), 2) Oliver to audit chat template concatenation to avoid double-eos boundaries, 3) Eva to run quant baseline comparing eos emission rates across fp16/q4 for the model.
Maya: I'll open PR for the streaming id-collapse and include a test that simulates `[.., 50256, 50256, 15496]` and checks we don't early-stop.
Oliver: leave a note in onboarding checklist to validate `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_string` roundtrip and to run `tokenizer.encode("\n\n")` checks.
Eva: and add a short eval to our regression suite: sample prompts with trailing blank lines and assert generation length/coverage.
Maya: thanks, will do. cc @Raj if you can review the PR when ready. :thanks:
